title: The Field That Was Quiet
subtitle: 历史事件 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史事件（历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史事件（历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：battle　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 battle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my grandfather was taken to see ① a battle that had ended eighty years before, and he said the field was the quietest place he had ever stood in. The ② battle, meaning the fighting and not the field, lasted nine hours and was decided in the last eleven minutes; a battle, he said, is the only event that is remembered by the ground and not by the people.

Every ③ battle in that valley was fought over the same road, and the ④ battle of 1866, meaning the one in the rain and not either of those, is the only one anybody in the town can name. A battle, my grandmother said, is nine parts road and one part weather; my grandfather said the road is the part that never changes.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ battle was the whole of the winter, meaning the argument and not the fighting. The ⑥ battle, meaning the struggle and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody wins and nobody enjoys; a battle, she said, is either something fought on a field or the only word that means both a war and a Tuesday. He said the Tuesday is the harder half.

By 1963 the ⑦ battle had become a name on a sign, and the sign had become an argument about how many had died. The ⑧ battle of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in April, was nine hours of ground and eighty years of quiet; a battle, he said, is either the fighting in the valley or the reason the road is still there. She said the road has always been the point.

The ⑨ battle I remember is the one in the rain, which nobody in the family fought and everybody in the family described. A ⑩ battle, my mother said in 1966, is the only thing that improves by being remembered; every battle, she said, is a road that has agreed to look like a story. He said the story was never the road.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 战役（指那场仗，与那片战场相对）
C. 固定搭配：be taken to see a battle 被带去看一场战役（旧址）
D. n. 战役（指那个山谷里每一场）
E. n. 战役（指 1866 年那一场）
F. n. 争斗；较量（指那年冬天的争吵）
G. n. 争斗（抽象：那种挣扎）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a battle that had ended eighty years before
The battle, meaning the fighting and not the field
battle was the whole of the winter
the battle had become a name on a sign
The battle of the whole thing
A battle, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: be taken to see a battle 意为“被带去看一场战役（旧址）”，1948 年祖父被带去看一场八十年前就结束了的战役。
battle 意为“战役”，指那场打仗而不是那片战场，它打了九小时，最后十一分钟决出胜负。
battle 指那个山谷里每一场战役，每一场都是为同一条路打的。
battle 指 1866 年那一场（在雨里打的那一场），是镇上唯一有人叫得出名字的。
battle 意为“争斗、较量”，指那年冬天的争吵，母亲说 battle 就是那年冬天的全部。
battle 为抽象用法，指那种挣扎，是一家人人人都赢、却没人觉得痛快的斗争。
battle 意为“战役”，到 1963 年这个 battle 成了牌子上的一个名字。
battle 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖父四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九小时的战地和八十年的安静。
battle 意为“战役”，我记得的是雨里那一场，家里没人打过，却人人都描述过。
battle 为抽象总称，母亲说战役是唯一会因为被记住而变好的事。
